description: A single temperature–time schematic (thermal-history / process-route diagram) for Fe–Mn–Al–C steel, drawn with a vertical axis labelled "Temperature" and a horizontal axis labelled "Time"; neither axis carries numeric tick marks. The traced profile begins by heating to a flat plateau labelled "1100-1200 °C" and "Solution", then descends through a zigzag segment labelled "Hot rolling" (the zigzag signifying multiple rolling passes), falls to a lower level marked by a smaller zigzag labelled "Cold rolling", and then branches into four alternative continuation routes marked by coloured arrows. Above the upper flat plateaus of the annealing step the labels read "1100-1200 °C" and "Annealing", with "600-800 °C" beneath; the final low-temperature plateau is labelled "450-700 °C" and "Aging". The four arrowed routes are: green "Route 1", red "Route 2", light-blue "Route 3" and purple dashed "Route 4". The schematic is a set of labelled processing regimes, not measured data; it has no scale bar and no numeric data values beyond the printed temperature ranges.

observations.observation: The figure is a Temperature (vertical axis) versus Time (horizontal axis) schematic; neither axis shows numeric tick values.
The initial high-temperature step is a flat plateau labelled 'Solution' at '1100-1200 °C'.
A descending zigzag segment is labelled 'Hot rolling', and a lower zigzag segment is labelled 'Cold rolling'.
Two annealing temperature levels are printed: '1100-1200 °C' and beneath it '600-800 °C', both marked 'Annealing'.
The final low-temperature plateau is labelled '450-700 °C' and 'Aging'.
Four alternative continuation routes are marked by coloured arrows: green 'Route 1', red 'Route 2', light-blue 'Route 3', and purple dashed 'Route 4'.
The caption states these are the regimes of hot and cold rolling, annealing and aging of Fe–Mn–Al–C steel.
The citing text states that Route 1 is rapid cooling to room temperature after hot rolling, followed by isothermal annealing and aging.
The citing text states that Route 2 uses cold rolling and recrystallization annealing to adapt the size and texture of δ-ferrite and κ-carbide.

The citing text states that aging at 500–700 °C for 0.5–2 h (routes 3 and 4) benefits nucleation of nanodispersed precipitates; note this 500–700 °C range differs from the 450-700 °C printed on the panel.
The citing text notes that cold rolling and recrystallization annealing are used because δ-ferrite in hot-rolled steel treated by simple cooling tends to have a coarse and banded morphology.

subfigures.description: Temperature (y) vs Time (x) process-route schematic for Fe–Mn–Al–C steel, with no numeric axis ticks. A profile rises to a 'Solution' plateau at 1100-1200 °C, descends through a zigzag 'Hot rolling' segment, drops to a lower zigzag 'Cold rolling' step, then splits into four coloured arrowed routes (green Route 1, red Route 2, light-blue Route 3, purple-dashed Route 4) passing through 'Annealing' plateaus marked 1100-1200 °C and 600-800 °C and an 'Aging' plateau marked 450-700 °C.
